message:
exp(apk): C r4 keep-prefix PROTOTYPE -- an overflow with no IDR keeps the queue that provably continues the codec's chain, cuts the newest instead; slot backpressure and one residence budget; behind a runtime switch that is OFF (keepalive-r2 e, apk-decoder-inbox C r4, Codex codex_apk_inbox_prefix_design_go_r1.md)

Experiment branch exp/apk-inbox-prefix from 2b492ef (C r3, kept as it is). Default unchanged: the switch is set only by
AndroidVideoDecoderSink::SetPrefixPolicyForTest; nothing in the product turns it on.

With the switch ON:
- case 3' (decoder_chain_inbox.hpp Trim): no IDR in the inbox AND the owner's proof (SetFrontier before each Offer): the
  codec's chain intact since a committed IDR (chainValid_: set at an IDR's CommitQueue, cleared on any loss the decoder
  sees, a codec reset, an inbox clear, an invalidation), the head = the newest AU the worker took + 1 (frontier), every
  queued AU the next of the one before it (the host stamps ++encodedSeq per AU: a hole is an AU never delivered), one
  generation, the head within the residence budget -> keep the prefix, drop the NEWEST until it fits (tail loss: the
  gap opens after it, the recovery asks as for any loss -- not an IDR commit, not a gate payment). Else: case 3.
- backpressure (the worker): nothing is popped while the pending slot holds a frame (the next one would only replace /
  lose it); the wait predicate does not wake on a queue behind a held frame (no hot loop) -- the 3 ms pump retries it.
- one residence budget: kInboxMaxFrames / target fps, clamped to [250, 500] ms (30 fps -> 267 ms); checked at the
  overflow (head too old -> case 3), at the Pop (an expired delta: a loss at its seq, MarkLoss trims to the next IDR),
  at the slot (an expired held delta dropped: a loss). An IDR never expires; a frame inside a codec call is not
  expirable. enqueueUs is now set always (was trace-only).
- DebugStatus: prefixPolicy prefixKept prefixKeptFrames tailLost prefixRefused ageExpPop ageExpSlot backpressure passes.

Test (new) android_decoder_inbox_prefix_test 21/21, 20/20 repeats: the product sink + stand-in NDK, the SAME schedule for
both policies (one binary), judged by an independent oracle over what the codec was handed (NAL type + the AU seq each
test frame carries): P0 no loss identical; P1 burst while the codec is busy: decodable 7 -> 15, corrupt 0 both; P2 no
buffer 150 ms: backpressure, 7 -> 11, passes at the pump rate; P3 no buffer 700 ms: no AU older than the budget fed
(12 stale, 0 fed), corrupt 0; P4 an IDR during a kept prefix; P5 a reset during a kept prefix: no delta to the new
codec before an IDR; P6 / P6b a hole inside / right after the frontier: not provable -> case 3; P7 sustained overload:
inbox <= 8, asks <= 4, back to the newest AU. The stand-in emits the first picture (else the sink's bootstrap replay
re-feeds an old IDR mid-schedule -- seen once as a corrupt input in a today's-C run before this).
Mutants (one condition each): no contiguity -> P6 corrupt; no frontier -> P6b corrupt; no age -> P3 (stale fed);
no backpressure -> P2; no chain invalidation -> nothing here fails (not shown).
Regression with the switch OFF (14 tests): chain 51, r2 contrast 2, merge 8, inbox 12, inbox_c 44, session 26, owed 32,
geometry 10, binding 17, decode_stats 42, liveness 68, session_liveness 9, pending_slot 21, idr_recovery 49 -- exit 0.
No device, no AVD, no product default change.
